title: Logotic Programming extensions: Glyphic Checksum, semantic spans, virality
description: Logotic Programming modules specify instruments: Glyphic Checksum invariants (#426, #1302), which #1302 claims cannot be extracted, misattributed or flattened; semantic spans (#444); a drift metric (#495); and virality measures (#564), which holds that correction amplifies a viral object. The Space Ark papers (#556, #559) claim a reconstruction theorem and that dense formal objects induce more procedural LLM behavior; The Missing Layer (#34) forecasts that prompt-native runtimes grow more relevant. The page also holds unrelated claims, from the Baal effigy to classifier interruption.

### 5.4.10 Branch-level collapse measurement (NEW v0.6 — LABOR)

Noise collapse does not first appear as one obviously bad text. It appears *statistically across descendants*. Each probationary branch is audited for:

- **Root retention.** Can blind readers (or models) correctly identify the root family above chance from the descendant? Too much retention = sterile imitation; too little = lineage loss. Calibrated interval.
